proposals.title: Zoom out from your video to the YouTube page; cursor lands on the description link
proposals.why: The whole comp: the full-frame video leaves through the top as the watch page rises and scales 86 → 100 % (2.17 s, long glide), a cursor settles on the first link, then a hard cut back to the video with a 0.2 s blur-to-sharp.
proposals.call: youtubeZoomOutLink(comp, {at, video, title: "Claude + Instagram = $32,561", channel: "Tapa", subscribers: "17.7K subscribers", avatar, likes: "39", views: "4,334 views  Sep 28, 2026", lines: [cta, link, cta2, link2], target: "link", colors: {description: "#373737", text: "#f2f2f2", link: "#3dadd1"}, moveDuration: 2.17, cutBack: 2.6, returnBlur: 28})

proposals.title: Full-frame clip hands off to a page rising and zooming out
proposals.why: A rig of two nulls moves the page up 1067 px and scales it 86.11 → 100 % (out 17.76 % / in 98.94 %) while the clip, parented to it, leaves through the top: the 'zoom out to where this video lives' move.
proposals.call: zoomOutToPage(comp, {video, page, at, duration: 2.17, fromScale: 86.11, rise: 1067})

proposals.title: Retime a keyed move by dragging two comp markers
proposals.why: Expression on the page nulls: play key 1 → key 2 between comp markers “PAGE MOVE START” and “PAGE MOVE END”, keeping the easing, so an editor retimes without touching keys.
proposals.call: markerRetime(layer, path, {start: "PAGE MOVE START", end: "PAGE MOVE END"})
proposals.previewNote: The comp markers PAGE MOVE START / END aren't in the recipe, so the expression errors and the keys drive the move; the preview shows the page-rig move (without the video) that the markers would retime.

proposals.title: Cursor glides onto a target
proposals.why: CURSOR - Figma PDF travels from below the page (1170, 3112.5) to the link (534, 2108) over 2.07 s, out 20 % / in 88.08 %, rotation −10°, scale 425 %, soft drop shadow; no press.
proposals.call: cursorClick(comp, {to: [534, 2108], from: [1170, 3112.5], at: 0.2667, travel: 2.07, press: false})
proposals.previewNote: No useful isolated preview: the cursor is Cursor.pdf, which only exists in Elias's Mac Motion Library cache, so rebuilt here the part renders empty. The whole-comp GIF is kept.

proposals.title: Rack into focus on a cut
proposals.why: RETURN VIDEO comes back with Gaussian blur 28 → 0 in 0.2 s (out 20 % / in 70 %, Repeat Edge Pixels), so the cut back to the video lands soft-to-sharp.
proposals.overlaps: same id as dj3-views-counter defocusIn (there an adjustment layer, 40 → 0 in 0.3 s)
proposals.previewNote: The rack is only 0.2 s, so at 12 fps just one or two frames show the blur; the play icon (Play.pdf) is Mac-only, so the plate shows only its label.

proposals.title: Editable YouTube watch-page details
proposals.why: Title, round-cropped avatar, channel + subscribers, like/dislike and share pills, grey description box with views/date, two CTA lines and two links: a fake YouTube page built from text and shapes.
proposals.call: youtubeWatchPage(comp, {title, channel, subscribers, avatar, likes, views, lines: [...], links: [...]})
proposals.previewNote: Layers are #n stack positions in YouTube Page (everything but the cursor). The avatar (Tapa.jpg) and Share icon (Share.pdf) are Mac-only files, so they render empty here.

proposals.title: One null with colour controls that re-themes a template
proposals.why: CTRL - Global holds Description / Text / Link colour controls; fills and text animators inside the page precomp read them by expression, so the look changes from one place.
proposals.overlaps: none (style.jsx does this at build time; this does it live inside a comp)
proposals.previewNote: A rig, not a move: a static view of what CTRL - Global colours (description box, title, description text). Layers are #n stack positions in YouTube Page. The Link colour doesn't show (links render in the Text colour; see the breakdown).

proposals.title: Replaceable 16:9 video slot
proposals.why: A precomp with a #171717 plate, a play icon and “YOUR VIDEO · 16:9”, used twice (leave and return) so swapping one source updates both.
proposals.previewNote: The play icon (Play.pdf) only exists on Elias's Mac, so only the plate and the label show.
